406: /-- The diameter of a set in a metric space. To get controllable behavior even when the diameter
407: should be infinite, we express it in terms of the `ediam` -/
408: noncomputable def diam (s : Set α) : ℝ :=
409:   ENNReal.toReal (ediam s)
410: 
411: /-- The diameter of a set is always nonnegative -/
412: theorem diam_nonneg : 0 ≤ diam s :=
413:   ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
414: 
415: theorem diam_subsingleton (hs : s.Subsingleton) : diam s = 0 := by
416:   simp [diam, ediam_subsingleton hs]
417: 
418: /-- The empty set has zero diameter -/
419: @[simp]
420: theorem diam_empty : diam (∅ : Set α) = 0 :=
421:   diam_subsingleton subsingleton_empty
422: 
423: /-- A singleton has zero diameter -/
424: @[simp]
425: theorem diam_singleton : diam ({x} : Set α) = 0 :=
426:   diam_subsingleton subsingleton_singleton
427: 
428: @[to_additive (attr := simp)]
429: theorem diam_one [One α] : diam (1 : Set α) = 0 :=
430:   diam_singleton
431: 
432: -- Does not work as a simp-lemma, since {x, y} reduces to (insert y {x})
433: theorem diam_pair : diam ({x, y} : Set α) = dist x y := by
434:   simp only [diam, ediam_pair, dist_edist]
435: 
436: -- Does not work as a simp-lemma, since {x, y, z} reduces to (insert z (insert y {x}))
437: theorem diam_triple :
438:     diam ({x, y, z} : Set α) = max (max (dist x y) (dist x z)) (dist y z) := by
439:   simp only [diam, ediam_triple, dist_edist]
440:   rw [ENNReal.toReal_max, ENNReal.toReal_max] <;> apply_rules [ne_of_lt, edist_lt_top, max_lt]
441: 
442: /-- If the distance between any two points in a set is bounded by some constant `C`,
443: then `ENNReal.ofReal C` bounds the emetric diameter of this set. -/
444: theorem ediam_le_of_forall_dist_le {C : ℝ} (h : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, dist x y ≤ C) :
445:     ediam s ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C :=
446:   ediam_le fun x hx y hy => (edist_dist x y).symm ▸ ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal (h x hx y hy)
447: 
448: /-- If the distance between any two points in a set is bounded by some non-negative constant,
449: this constant bounds the diameter. -/
450: theorem diam_le_of_forall_dist_le {C : ℝ} (h₀ : 0 ≤ C) (h : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, dist x y ≤ C) :
451:     diam s ≤ C :=
452:   ENNReal.toReal_le_of_le_ofReal h₀ (ediam_le_of_forall_dist_le h)
453: 
454: /-- If the distance between any two points in a nonempty set is bounded by some constant,
455: this constant bounds the diameter. -/
456: theorem diam_le_of_forall_dist_le_of_nonempty (hs : s.Nonempty) {C : ℝ}
457:     (h : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, dist x y ≤ C) : diam s ≤ C :=
458:   have h₀ : 0 ≤ C :=
459:     let ⟨x, hx⟩ := hs
460:     le_trans dist_nonneg (h x hx x hx)
461:   diam_le_of_forall_dist_le h₀ h
462: 
463: /-- The distance between two points in a set is controlled by the diameter of the set. -/
464: theorem dist_le_diam_of_mem' (h : ediam s ≠ ⊤) (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s) :
465:     dist x y ≤ diam s := by
466:   rw [diam, dist_edist]
467:   exact ENNReal.toReal_mono h <| edist_le_ediam_of_mem hx hy
468: 
469: /-- Characterize the boundedness of a set in terms of the finiteness of its emetric.diameter. -/
